name: Orbit wrap

parameters.label: Path: rings / coil / atom / double coil / Saturn / gimbals / knot / crown / swarm / whirl
Cylinder / sphere / cone / hourglass / barrel / funnel
Band: tube / tape / twisted ribbon / beads / hairline / dashes / chain / zipper / double line / striped tape
Far arcs fade into the paper
One ink / near and far / stepped / blended / alternating
Subject: title only / solid / slab / glow / torus / pill / star / striped orb
Title shows through on the far arcs, mirrored

logic: Rings, a coil, crossed orbits or a double coil are wound round a vertical axis, seen by a raised camera and leaned in the page. The far half of every orbit is drawn first, then the subject (a solid on the orbit's own profile, a slab or a glow), then the poster type, then the near half of every orbit above it all, so the title sits inside the rings. Bands are round tubes, flat tape that shows its darker inside on the far arcs, twisted ribbon, beads or a hairline with satellites; inks run near/far, stepped or blended by turn, or alternate. Type mode prints the title on the near face of the band, foreshortened toward the sides, and can let it show through mirrored on the far arcs. Further paths: flat Saturn rings, nested gimbals, a torus knot, a wavy crown, a swarm of small orbits and a whirl; further bands: dashes, chain links, zipper teeth, double neon rails and striped tape; further subjects: torus, pill, faceted star and striped orb. The axis can bend, the band can taper, radii can jitter, turns can crowd toward one end, and echo trails, a drop shadow and out-of-focus far arcs finish it.
basis: Canonical source: Filmpodium "Marilyn Monroe Revisited", 2023 (census 0277): a thick two-colour coil wound round a figure, the near arcs over it and the far arcs behind. Also Journées de Soleure 2023 (0690, hoops round a column), Abstract (1062, a halo) and Mehrspur Pop & Jazz (1035, copy on a wound band).

name: Sawtooth and spring

parameters.label: Spring / stripes / fins / ring / spiral / waveform
Zigzag / sawtooth / square / sine / coil / pulse / stairs / bounce / noise
Compression toward the end (negative: the start)
Stripe depth (ring: 1 is a solid blade)
One ink / by band / by turn / blended along

logic: One waveform (zigzag with an adjustable lean, sawtooth, square, sine, looping coil, heartbeat pulse, stairs, bouncing arcs or seeded audio noise) is laid along a run: a straight or bent line, a ring or a spiral. Its turns can compress toward one end like a loaded spring and its swing can grow or shrink. It is drawn as a band (a spring with a cut, round, arrow or snake-head end, a sawblade or sun, a coiled spiral), as stripes that tile the field exactly, as rows of fins, or mirrored into a waveform; rows can recede. Every straight side or half period is a face: faces fold into two tones or shade from a dark base as a gradient, halftone or hatch. Bands taper and dash. Effects stack over the whole drawing: an extruded depth, a second ink printed out of register, and glitch slices. Rounded corners, a hand-drawn wobble, graph paper, neon glow, outlines and the title along the band finish it.
basis: Canonical source: Kevin Drumm at ECAL, 2018 (census 0255, credited to Notter+Vigne): one heavy zigzag stroke whose turns tighten toward the foot of the poster. Also Komet Soirée graphique (0702, a zigzag snake), Printemps culturel Neuchâtel (0029, chevron stripes), Claudia Basel (0262, shaded sawtooth fins), Volumes (0807, chevron arrows) and Neubad Luzern (0948, an outlined zigzag on graph paper).

logic: Circles are packed into a field until they kiss: the largest gap first (capped by a size that can fall off toward the edge or the centre, with ties going to snug places along a diagonal, at the centre, the edges or the foot), an Apollonian gasket, rolling rows of tangent circles that grow along the row, a golden-angle sunflower, or a hex lattice whose sizes follow a radial, linear, wave or random field. The field can be a rectangle, circle, arch, triangle or diamond. Sharp wedges run from the kissing points out through the gaps to the field edge. Every circle carries one mark (disc, ring, target, half moon, pac, shaded ball, halftone, hatch, flower or rounded square) in one ink or several. The field is filled, or the circles and wedges are punched out of it; a cut-paper shadow, a misregistered second printing, outlines and the title set one letter per circle finish it. Type sits inside the largest circles.
